incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT — SEV2: serving-runtime-usw2 high 5xx rate detected (AlertID PD-3221). Pagers sent to #incidents :rotating_light:

pager-duty-oncall: ACK — I'm on it. Starting triage and opening bridge.

alice (sre): Observing 5xx spike + tail latency ↑. Logs show repeated \"CUDA error: out of memory\" and \"nv_peer_memory: registration failed -22\" from model-serving pods. Not sure if primary cause is runtime or fabric yet.

bob (runtime): Pasting relevant tail from pod model-svc-7f9 (container xyz):
```
[2026-03-01T17:34:10Z] runtime: cudaSetDevice(0) -> CUDA error 700 (out of memory)
[2026-03-01T17:34:10Z] runtime: nv_peer_buf_map failed: -22
[2026-03-01T17:34:10Z] kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5e: port 1 link down
```

carla (infra): Hmm, mlx5 port flaps. Can someone run `ibstat` and `ethtool -S` on the affected host? We had noise on IB fabric earlier today.

dan (support): Customer reports intermittent timeouts during generation; retries often succeed. Affected: customer-acme (3% of requests), customer-beta (1%).

eve (eng): My hypothesis: RDMA path blips cause nv_peer registration to fail, the runtime falls back to copies or re-allocs, which increases memory pressure and triggers OOMs under heavy batching. Recommend isolating nodes showing mlx5 errors first.

alice (sre): Quick checks on rnode-14:
```
$ ssh rnode-14
$ dmesg | tail -n 50
[...]
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: firmware error recovered: link length mismatch
nv_peer_memory: failed to pin user buffer, rc=-11
```

carla (infra): ibstat output from rnode-14: 
```
CA 'mlx5_0'
    CA type: MT4099
    Number of ports: 2
    Port 1: Active
    Port 2: Down
```
`ethtool -S` shows elevated rx_err and tx_discards on IB ports. Looks like physical layer or SFP issue.

bob (runtime): Mitigation plan: cordon+drain rnode-14 and rnode-15 from serving pool, restart runtime containers on healthy nodes, temporarily reduce batch sizes. I'll start draining rnode-14 now.

alice (sre): Commands I'm running:
```
kubectl cordon rnode-14
kubectl drain rnode-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-serving --namespace=prod --field-selector=spec.nodeName=rnode-16
```

eve (eng): Also push a temporary routing fallback to cpu-backed replicas to drop GPU pressure:
```
redwood route update --service=model-serving --fallback=cpu-variant --pct=20
```

carla (infra): Notifying network ops. I see tor-ib-17 reporting port flaps for the rnode-14 link. I'm going to admin-down the port to force reroute while network team replaces SFP.

carla (infra): executed on switch mgmt: `interface port 1/17 shut` (will keep down until replacement).

bob (runtime): After drain+restart: restarted nodes show fewer CUDA OOMs but some nv_peer errors persist under bulk batching. Lowering batch size should help.

alice (sre): Pushed config change to reduce batching:
```
PATCH /config/model-serving
{
  "batching": {
    "max_tokens": 512,
    "max_batch": 8
  }
}
```

eve (eng): Also increased controller healthcheck grace window (retries=5, grace=60s) to avoid rapid pod flapping during transient fabric hiccups.

carla (infra): Network ops replaced SFP on tor-ib-17 and reports lower error counters post-replace. Keeping port admin-down until we validate.

bob (runtime): Observed results: 45m since page, 5xx rate dropped from 22% -> 1.2%. Tail latency improving. Rolling cpu-fallback down to 5% to confirm stability. :white_check_mark:

dan (support): Customer-acme confirms generation is back to normal on their end. Marking impacted list: customer-acme, customer-beta. Sending status update to customers now.

pager-duty-oncall: Preparing handoff — my rotation ends in 20m. @alice will take over. Summary and follow-up list coming.

alice (sre): Incident summary for handoff: 
- start_ts: 1768009876
- symptoms: ↑5xx, CUDA OOMs, nv_peer_memory rc errors, IB port flaps
- likely root cause: intermittent IB fabric faults -> RDMA registration failures -> runtime fallback/amplified memory pressure -> OOMs under load
- actions taken: cordoned/drained rnode-14/15, restarted runtimes, reduced batching, enabled cpu fallback, replaced SFP on tor-ib-17, increased healthcheck grace, routed fraction to cpu-variant
- customer impact: partial request failures for ~35 minutes for two customers, transient latency increase for many customers
- follow-ups: deep-dive with network team on switch logs & IB counters, add automated alerting for nv_peer errors, run soak tests for high-batch traffic, update runbook for IB flap response

alice (sre): Handoff to @frank (sre) for next oncall. Leaving bridge open for 30m.

frank (sre): ACK — taking over. I'll validate metrics, review logs, and pick up the postmortem draft.

incident-bot: Incident PD-3221 marked as mitigated at 1768010321 by pager-duty-oncall. Postmortem assigned to alice (sre), carla (infra), bob (runtime). Severity: SEV2. :telephone_receiver:

pager-duty-oncall: Closing notes: follow-up meeting scheduled tomorrow 14:00 UTC; action owner assignments to be tracked in ticket INF-4582. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
